banner_firstperson: Qualitative visualization — trajectory calculations remain relativistic.
planck_message:
PLANCK-CURVATURE THRESHOLD REACHED.
CLASSICAL GENERAL RELATIVITY IS NO LONGER RELIABLE.
NO EXPERIMENTALLY VERIFIED THEORY DETERMINES THE CONTINUATION.

metadata.integrator: Dormand–Prince RK5(4), adaptive, FSAL, PI step control; independent variable ln r inside (tau outside when needed)
metadata.internal_units: geometrized G = c = 1, M = 1: length unit GM/c^2, time unit GM/c^3, r_s = 2

config.integrator: Dormand–Prince RK5(4), adaptive, FSAL, PI step control; independent variable ln r inside (tau outside when needed)
config.notes: Default scenario: radial free fall from rest at infinity (E = 1, L = 0), started numerically at r0 = 100 r_s. Validated trajectory stops at r_QG where K = 1/l_P^4.

relative_uncertainties.note: geometrized results (in units of GM/c^2, GM/c^3) carry no constant uncertainty at all

regimes.note: Regime labels are a display convention (see physics_notes.md §9); the physics is identical classical GR everywhere up to r_QG, where the validated integration STOPS.

metadata.kruskal_time_origin_note: Kruskal/Penrose coordinates use the Schwarzschild time translation that puts the horizon crossing at v = 0 (V_K = 1); this is an exact symmetry of the metric.

milestones.label: ISCO (r = 6GM/c^2 = 3 r_s)
milestones.note: innermost stable circular orbit; traversed radially (not an orbit here)

milestones.label: Event horizon (r = r_s = 2GM/c^2)
milestones.note: future event horizon; regular in ingoing EF coordinates

milestones.label: Curvature beyond direct experimental tests
milestones.note: K^(-1/4) = 10000 m: onset of 'CLASSICAL GR — EXTREME CURVATURE' label (labelling convention, see physics_notes.md)

milestones.label: Planck-curvature threshold r_QG (K = 1/l_P^4)
milestones.note: END OF VALIDATED CLASSICAL GR; no experimentally verified theory determines the continuation

signal_timeline.note: Distant-observer received-signal timeline (EXACT GR RESULT evaluated on the validated numerical worldline; exterior only). eps = r/r_s - 1 of the emission event; t_receive_years = reception-time interval on a distant static observer's clock between the radial signal emitted at the start and the one emitted at this event, (u - u_start) GM/c^3 with u = v - 2 r_*; one_plus_z = frequency ratio emitted/received for that radially outgoing signal (= du/dtau); tau_years = emitter proper time since the start; t_schw_years = Schwarzschild coordinate time of emission since the start event. As eps -> 0, 1+z grows as exp(u/4M) (e-folding time late_time_efold_years = 4GM/c^3), t_receive -> infinity while tau converges to the finite horizon-crossing proper time. Signals emitted at r <= r_s never reach the observer (not listed). Julian years.

speculative.menu_title: SPECULATIVE QUANTUM-GRAVITY TOY MODELS — NOT ESTABLISHED PHYSICS
speculative.note: Each toy model is integrated with the project's EF geodesic code in its first-integral (E, L) form, in units of the core length; only f(r) differs from the Schwarzschild cross-check formulation. These toy integrations are NOT validated physics. The choice of core length is arbitrary (1e4 Planck lengths here) and has NO observational basis. Inner-horizon instabilities (mass inflation) are ignored. These curves must never be read as predictions.

hayward.parameter_note: integrated in units of the core length l; mu = M/l
hayward.formulation: first integrals (E = 1, L = 0), ln r independent variable; see comment in run_model
hayward.reaches_r0_in_finite_proper_time: no (de Sitter core: r ~ exp(-tau/l), asymptotic approach)

hayward.metric: ds^2 = -f dv^2 + 2 dv dr + r^2 dOmega^2,  f = 1 - 2 M r^2/(r^3 + 2 M l^2)
hayward.citation: Hayward, S. A., Phys. Rev. Lett. 96, 031103 (2006)
hayward.assumptions: static, spherically symmetric, one free length l; matter content is an effective anisotropic fluid violating the strong energy condition in the core
hayward.differs_from_GR: f -> 1 - r^2/l^2 (de Sitter) as r -> 0 instead of -2M/r; curvature bounded, K_max ~ O(1/l^4); inner horizon near r ~ l
hayward.observational_support: NONE — l is unobservable for any astrophysical black hole (exterior indistinguishable from Schwarzschild)

bardeen.citation: Bardeen (1968) GR5, Tbilisi; Ayón-Beato & García, Phys. Lett. B 493, 149 (2000)
bardeen.assumptions: static, spherically symmetric; sourced by a nonlinear-electrodynamics magnetic monopole of charge g
bardeen.differs_from_GR: de Sitter core, finite curvature; inner horizon

dymnikova.assumptions: static, spherically symmetric; vacuum-like anisotropic fluid with p_r = -rho
dymnikova.differs_from_GR: de Sitter core with density rho_0 = 3/(8 pi r_0^2); exterior deviation exponentially small
